plain: If you're in the Bay Area, Lake Tahoe is your easiest option, roughly a three-to-four-hour drive. Palisades Tahoe (formerly Squaw Valley) has big terrain and a lively base village, while Heavenly spans California and Nevada with sweeping lake views from the summit. Northstar suits families and intermediate skiers, with a walkable village for apres-ski. Kirkwood tends to get deeper snow and has a quieter, more advanced feel, and Sugar Bowl is smaller and convenient if you want to dodge weekend crowds. If you're willing to drive about five hours, Mammoth Mountain has a long season and often holds snow well into spring. Book lift tickets in advance, since weekends sell out fast.

plain: Great options include chunky triangular crayons and grip-friendly pencils designed for small hands, since they encourage the right pincer grip before switching to standard pencils. Wooden puzzles with letter or number shapes help kids trace forms with their fingers first. Magnetic or wooden tracing boards with sand or salt trays let children practice letters by feel, which builds muscle memory without the pressure of getting it perfect on paper. Chalkboards and dry-erase boards are forgiving for repeated practice, and lacing cards or playdough strengthen the same hand muscles used in writing. Apps and tablets with stylus tracing games can also help, though hands-on tools tend to build fine motor control more effectively for younger children.

plain: Several national capitals start with S. In Europe, there's Stockholm (Sweden), Sofia (Bulgaria), Skopje (North Macedonia), and San Marino (San Marino). In Asia, Seoul (South Korea) and Singapore (Singapore) both qualify. In the Americas, there's Santiago (Chile), San Salvador (El Salvador), San Jose (Costa Rica), and Sucre (Bolivia's constitutional capital). Suva, the capital of Fiji, and Sana'a, the capital of Yemen, round things out from Oceania and the Middle East. That's a solid spread across continents, from Nordic Stockholm to island-nation Suva, showing how common the letter S is among world capitals.

plain: Classic comfort breakfasts built around eggs include a loaded breakfast burrito with scrambled eggs, cheese, potatoes, and salsa wrapped in a warm tortilla. Eggs Benedict, with poached eggs and hollandaise over an English muffin and Canadian bacon, feels indulgent for a weekend morning. A Southern-style plate of eggs over easy with buttered grits, biscuits, and sausage gravy is deeply comforting too. Shakshuka, eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce, is warming and great with crusty bread for dipping. For something simpler, a fried egg on buttered toast with crispy bacon and hash browns hits the same nostalgic notes without much effort.

plain: Princess Elowen slipped away from the castle gardens one grey afternoon, chasing a fox that vanished into the hillside. Behind a curtain of ivy, she found a cave mouth she had never noticed before. Inside, her lantern lit walls etched with old carvings of a kingdom that predated her family's rule, and a narrow passage led deeper underground. She followed it nervously, heart pounding, until it opened into a chamber holding a dusty chest. Inside lay a crown far older than her own, along with a letter explaining that her ancestors had once shared this land peacefully with its first people. Elowen carried the crown home, and used the story to convince her father to protect the hillside as a historic site rather than build on it.

plain: Most humans have 20 total fingers if you count both hands and both feet, since fingers and toes are both digits, but if you mean just the hands, the answer is 10: five on each hand. Each hand typically has a thumb plus four fingers, adding up to five digits per hand. Some people are born with a condition called polydactyly, giving them one or more extra digits on a hand or foot, while others lose fingers to injury or are born with fewer due to genetic conditions, so the count can vary. But for the vast majority of people without such differences, 10 fingers on the hands is the standard number most references use.

plain: Before bringing a puppy home, puppy-proof your space by removing chewable hazards, blocking off stairs, and securing loose cords. Stock up on essentials: a crate for training, a comfortable bed, food and water bowls, age-appropriate puppy food, a collar with an ID tag, and a leash. Chew toys are essential for teething, and enzymatic cleaner is a must for inevitable accidents during house training. Schedule a vet visit early for vaccinations and a wellness check, and consider pet insurance while your puppy is young and healthy. Start basic training and socialization right away, exposing your puppy to new people, sounds, and situations. Finally, set a consistent feeding and potty schedule, since routine helps puppies learn faster.

plain: Henry Ford's Model T was famously offered only in black from about 1914 to 1925, mainly because of manufacturing efficiency rather than aesthetic preference. Black japan enamel paint dried faster than other colored paints available at the time, which mattered enormously once Ford introduced the moving assembly line. A faster-drying, durable paint meant cars could move through production without bottlenecks, keeping pace with the line's speed and lowering costs. Ford wanted to build cars quickly and cheaply enough for average Americans to afford, and standardizing on one color simplified sourcing, application, and quality control. Interestingly, earlier and later Model T years did offer other colors, so the all-black era was really a deliberate efficiency choice tied to peak mass production.
